title: Tobin and Nell's Night Magic
markdown:
High on the tall tall mountains, where the snow lay like a gentle blanket and the stars twinkled close as tiny friendly eyes, lived two friends. Tobin was a wizard with a heart full of warmth. His robe had little silver stars. He carried a smooth stick that felt warm in his hand. His very special friend was a breath of air, so soft it was like a happy sigh. The whisper-wind.

Tobin’s friend was Nell. Nell had hair like the deep blue sky, and little bells in her hair that tinkled like soft secrets when she moved. Her dearest friend was a tiny light, a glow-worm that shone with a kind steady light, like a little lamp of happy thoughts.

One evening the moon climbed high, painting the snow with soft silver. Tobin and Nell sat near the edge of the sleepy moonlit trees. They wanted to show each other their special friends. Cool air. Pine needles. Sleepy earth. A beautiful moon-moth, wings like shimmery lace, floated silently nearby, watching with big dark eyes. It seemed to dance on the soft whispers of the wind.

“I will show you first,” said Tobin, voice as soft as falling snow. He held out his warm stick and whispered to his whisper-wind. A little puff of air, no bigger than a sleepy breath, swirled around them. It tickled the little bell-flowers that grew even in the cold. They all began to chime, a quiet musical sound, like tiny silver bells far away. The moon-moth, curious, fluttered a little closer, wings catching the moonlight.

Nell smiled. Eyes like far-off stars.

“That was lovely, Tobin.” Voice like a gentle rustle of leaves. “Now, watch this.” She held out her hand, soft and curved like a little nest. Her glow-worm, nestled there, began to shine. It wove a pattern of light, a little swirling star-picture right above her hand. Peaceful to watch, that steady friendly glow. The moon-moth dipped and swayed, as if dancing to the glow-worm’s quiet song.

Tobin clapped his hands softly, like the lightest patter of rain.

“Oh, Nell, that’s so wonderful.” He thought about his next special friend, a tiny creature made of sparkling ice. He gently wiggled his warm stick.

Then the beautiful moon-moth, perhaps a little too excited by all the lovely light, gave a gentle flutter. A soft breeze swirled, not a strong one, just a little more airy than before. The breeze made the moon-moth’s wings shimmer. As it danced near Nell’s hand, its shimmery wings cast a dappled light that made the glow-worm’s light even more beautiful. It seemed to add its own soft silvery shine to everything.

Tobin and Nell looked at each other, eyes wide. A soft sigh seemed to move through the trees, only the ordinary kind, pine and snow.

Then Nell started to giggle, light and happy, like tiny bells.

“Oh, little moon-moth. You are making our special friends’ magic even more beautiful.”

Tobin smiled, warm and bright.

“You’re right, Nell. Perhaps our friends’ magic is even more lovely when it all plays together.” He looked at the moon-moth, and the moon-moth seemed to understand, tilting its delicate head. It hovered gently.

Tobin whispered to his whisper-wind, and Nell held out her glow-worm. This time the whisper-wind did not scatter anything. It gently swirled the air, lifting the moon-moth’s soft light. A beautiful dance of light. The moon-moth danced just above, silver wings shimmering, sprinkling tiny sleepy dust of moonlight. Nell’s glow-worm shone its steady light, a warm beacon. The bell-flowers, touched by the gentle breezes and the moon-moth’s light, began to chime their sweet faraway melody.

It was not a contest anymore. It was a gentle dance of light and sound, woven from moonbeams, soft chimes, and steady glows. The moon-moth settled on a low branch, wings still faintly shimmering, a quiet watcher. Tobin and Nell sat together, watching the last of the soft magic fade into the quiet night, feeling warm and content.

“That was the most beautiful magic ever,” whispered Tobin.

“Yes,” agreed Nell, snuggling closer. “And the moon-moth helped.”

The moon began its slow journey down, long peaceful shadows like sleeping giants. Tobin and Nell yawned, big and wide and warm. Cool air. Pine needles. Soft snow. Time for rest. The moon-moth blinked its soft light, as if saying goodnight. Soon all the gentle magic of the mountains would settle into slumber. Tucked in their warm thoughts, Tobin and Nell drifted off, dreaming of moonbeams and soft chimes and the gentle dance of light. The bells in Nell’s hair went quiet. Tobin’s stick stayed warm in his hand, even after the whisper-wind had gone to sleep.
